front: What is the **circular flow of income**?
back: A model showing how money, goods, services and factors move between households, firms, the government, the financial sector and the rest of the world.

front: What is the condition for equilibrium national income?
back: Injections equal leakages: I + G + X = S + T + M.

front: What happens if injections exceed leakages?
back: Spending exceeds output, firms expand and national income rises until leakages equal injections.

front: What happens if leakages exceed injections?
back: Spending falls short of output, stocks build up, firms cut output and national income falls.
It is income not spent on domestic output, although banks lend it for investment.
A closed economy has no foreign trade; an open one has exports (injection) and imports (leakage).

front: Give two limitations of the circular flow model.
back: It does not explain why injections and leakages change, and it ignores prices and time lags.
